patient.chief_complaint: Worst headache of life while exercising at gym, vomiting, neck stiffness
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Thompson is a 54-year-old woman with hypertension and active smoking who presents to the emergency department with a classic subarachnoid hemorrhage presentation. She was on the elliptical machine at the gym when she developed an instantaneous, explosive headache she rates as 10/10, unlike anything she has experienced before. She immediately vomited, dropped to the ground, and was helped by gym staff who called 911. She remained conscious throughout. On EMS arrival, her blood pressure was 198/116 mmHg. She arrives with severe headache, neck stiffness, photophobia, and one additional vomiting episode en route. She has no prior history of severe headaches. She denies focal weakness, vision loss, or loss of consciousness. Risk factors are classic: hypertension, smoking, and a family history of aneurysm. Hunt-Hess Grade 2 on arrival.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4; GCS 15; severe photophobia; grimacing from pain
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: PERRL 3mm, brisk; EOM intact; no ptosis; fundoscopy: bilateral disc margins sharp, no papilledema; visual fields full
neurological_exam.motor: 5/5 strength all four extremities; no pronator drift
neurological_exam.sensory: Intact to light touch and pinprick
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ and symmetric throughout; plantar responses flexor bilaterally
neurological_exam.additional: Marked nuchal rigidity: chin-to-chest restricted 5 cm; Kernig sign positive bilaterally; Brudzinski sign positive; Hunt-Hess Grade 2

findings.description: Thick hyperdense blood filling suprasellar cistern and interpeduncular fossa

ct.impression: 1. Subarachnoid hemorrhage, Fisher grade 3, with thick hyperdense blood filling the basal cisterns, bilateral Sylvian fissures, and anterior interhemispheric fissure. 2. No intraparenchymal hemorrhage. 3. No hydrocephalus. CTA head and neck recommended for vascular evaluation. Clinical correlation recommended.
recommended_actions: CTA head and neck recommended for vascular evaluation

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: WBC 15.6 x10^9/L (H), Glucose 162 mg/dL (H), Troponin I 0.24 ng/mL (H), BNP 198 pg/mL (H).

csf.appearance: Grossly bloody, uniform bright red across tubes 1-4

special_tests.Xanthochromia: Present - visible yellow supernatant and spectrophotometry confirmed

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 28 cmH2O. WBC: 360/uL corrected (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 222 mg/dL (markedly elevated). Glucose: 82 mg/dL (serum 162, ratio 0.51 - normal) (ratio 0.51). Xanthochromia: Present - visible yellow supernatant and spectrophotometry confirmed.

findings: Deep symmetric T-wave inversions V1-V5 (neurogenic pattern)
ecg.interpretation: Sinus tachycardia, rate 102. Deep symmetric T-wave inversions in V1–V5. QTc prolonged at 494 ms. No ST-segment elevation. No pathological Q waves. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Saccular aneurysm 6.8 x 5.6 mm with irregular lobulation and daughter sac - clearly ruptured

output.impression: 1. Saccular aneurysm of the anterior communicating artery, measuring 6.8 x 5.6 mm, with irregular lobulation, a daughter sac, and a 3.8 mm neck. 2. No additional intracranial aneurysms. Findings are consistent with the source of subarachnoid hemorrhage. Conventional DSA recommended for treatment planning. Clinical correlation recommended.
recommended_actions: Conventional DSA recommended for treatment planning

output.wall_motion: Apical hypokinesis with basal hyperkinesis - Takotsubo pattern
output.impression: 1. Left ventricular ejection fraction 46%, mildly reduced. 2. Apical hypokinesis with basal hyperkinesis — Takotsubo (stress) cardiomyopathy pattern. 3. Trace mitral regurgitation. Consider repeat echocardiogram in 4–6 weeks to assess recovery of systolic function. Clinical correlation recommended.
recommended_actions: Consider repeat echocardiogram in 4–6 weeks to assess recovery of systolic function

output.impression: Moderate-to-severe bilateral vasospasm. Bilateral ACA mean flow velocities 156–164 cm/s, Lindegaard ratios 4.8–5.2. Bilateral MCA mean flow velocities 138–148 cm/s, Lindegaard ratios 3.4–3.8. Basilar velocity within normal limits. CT perfusion recommended for hemodynamic correlation. Clinical correlation recommended.
recommended_actions: CT perfusion recommended for hemodynamic correlation

interactions: Amlodipine + nimodipine: significant additive calcium channel blockade - enhanced hypotension
warnings: Monitor BP before each nimodipine dose
Amlodipine has long half-life (30-50 hours) - effects persist 2-3 days after last dose

findings.description: Large perfusion deficit without established infarction yet

output.impression: Severe bilateral anterior circulation perfusion compromise. Critically reduced cerebral blood flow (22–28 mL/100g/min) bilaterally. Reduced cerebral blood volume in bilateral anterior circulation indicating tissue at risk. Large perfusion–infarction mismatch in bilateral frontal lobes. No established infarction. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.query: Smoking tobacco cerebral aneurysm SAH risk secondary prevention

results.finding: Smoking doubles or triples risk of SAH; relative risk 2-3x
Smoking promotes aneurysm growth and rupture via inflammatory and vascular mechanisms
Smoking cessation reduces SAH risk and aneurysm growth rate
Smoking cessation is class I recommendation for aneurysm patients

output.summary: Tobacco smoking is associated with a 2–3-fold increased risk of subarachnoid hemorrhage from intracranial aneurysm rupture. Smoking promotes aneurysm formation, growth, and rupture through inflammatory and vascular mechanisms. Major societal guidelines classify smoking cessation as a class I recommendation for patients with intracranial aneurysms. Evidence supports pharmacotherapy as an adjunct to cessation counseling in high-risk populations. Clinical correlation recommended.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from anterior communicating artery aneurysm (Hunt-Hess 2, Fisher 3)

differential.key_features: CT shows thick SAH; CSF non-clearing bloody with xanthochromia; CTA shows AComA aneurysm
CT shows focal SAH not diffuse edema; aneurysm confirmed; meningism present
CSF bloody with xanthochromia not neutrophilic; no fever; glucose ratio normal

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Thick SAH in basal cisterns and bilateral Sylvian fissures

optimal_actions.action: Interpret labs - stress leukocytosis, troponin, coagulation
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Neurogenic cardiac injury pattern, normal coagulation
Deep symmetric T inversions V1-V5, QTc 494 ms - neurogenic pattern

optimal_actions.action: Check nimodipine + amlodipine interaction - HOLD amlodipine
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Hold amlodipine - additive calcium channel blockade

critical_actions: CTA identifies AComA aneurysm - expedite treatment
Hold amlodipine before starting nimodipine - significant interaction
Nimodipine 60 mg q4h x21 days from diagnosis
ICU admission with continuous cardiac monitoring (QTc 494 ms)
Smoking cessation counseling - class I recommendation
contraindicated_actions: Do not continue amlodipine with nimodipine - additive hypotension
Do not delay aneurysm treatment - rebleed risk 20-30% in 24 hours
key_reasoning_points: Classic triad: sudden worst headache, vomiting, neck stiffness = SAH until proven otherwise
Risk factor profile: hypertension + smoking + family history = very high SAH risk
Fisher grade 3 SAH predicts high vasospasm risk - daily TCD monitoring days 4-14 essential
AComA is the most common aneurysm causing SAH - basal cistern and interhemispheric blood distribution
Amlodipine (long-acting CCB) + nimodipine (CCB) = significant hypotension risk - hold amlodipine
Neurogenic T-wave inversions (deep, symmetric, no ST elevation) are classic SAH ECG pattern
Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (EF 46%) requires monitoring but is usually reversible over weeks
